QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_26

question.text: Under SAS-400 the Workplace Gender-Wage-Gap indicator is computed as:

answer.text: Female median wage / Male median wage × 100
(Male median wage − Female median wage) / Male median wage × 100

explanation.text: The Logic: The standard gender wage gap is (Male − Female) / Male × 100. A gap of zero means parity; a positive gap means women earn less. Option B is female-to-male ratio (a related but inverse measure). Options C and A are not gaps. The Trap: Option B is the ratio (not the gap). Options C, A are irrelevant. Cross-Exam Context: Wage-gap computation also comes up in SEBI BRSR disclosure (III-A / III-C) and ILO-standard reporting. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Check whether the SE's 'wage gap' is computed for full-time equivalents — part-time female workforce concentration can exaggerate or understate the gap dramatically.
